RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel alongside an apparent qualification gap and delayed feedback raises legitimate concerns about implicit bias or in-group favoritism. However, it is not conclusive proof; senior municipal roles often heavily weigh interview performance, political acumen, and public consultation experience over technical credentials.

Raising gender bias directly at this stage carries high professional risk without documentation. First, send a polite follow-up requesting your interview scores and hiring criteria. If the municipality remains unresponsive or procedural irregularities appear, consult an employment lawyer or utilize public records requests to review the evaluation rubrics before deciding whether to raise bias formally.
